title: add NVTX ranges and microbench instrumentation for runtime profiling
author: Priya Raman
description: Add NVTX range annotations and a lightweight microbenchmark harness to the serving runtime to make kernel-level and scheduling hotspots visible in end-to-end traces and perf dashboards. Motivation: recent production perf regressions during peak burst traffic highlighted gaps in visibility - we could not correlate scheduler backpressure with kernel latency spikes. This PR introduces: 1) NVTX ranges around key runtime phases (request-deserialize, scheduling/enqueue, batch-assembly, kv-cache-lookup, forward-kernel, kv-cache-store, postprocess/serialize) with consistent naming and payloads; 2) per-inference counters (tokens_generated, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, batch_size_histogram) exported via existing metrics bridge; 3) a microbench binary (runtime_microbench) that can run synthetic workloads against a local runtime and emit structured perf events (+ nvtx) for uploading to our perf dashboard; 4) lightweight CI microbench smoke test to detect large regressions in kernel latency on PRs. Backwards compatibility: NVTX calls are guarded by a runtime flag and compiled out on builds without NVTX to avoid perf cost in builds that don't need tracing. See release_notes for rollout guidance and how to use the new microbench tool.

ci_checks: microbench-smoke: run small workload in CI (pass)
release_notes: Added runtime NVTX ranges and a microbenchmark tool for kernel/scheduler visibility. How to use: enable telemetry.nvtx in runtime config, run tools/runtime_microbench with --workload=kv-heavy or --workload=gen-heavy, upload perf events to the perf dashboard. This is an observability-only change guarded by a feature flag; no functional behavior change expected.
notes_for_operators: Rollout: enable NVTX on canary Dedicated clusters first. NVTX is disabled by default for low-overhead production builds. The microbench binary is intended for perf engineering. Metrics exported: runtime.tokens_generated, runtime.kv_cache_hits, runtime.kv_cache_misses, runtime.batch_size. Dashboards: observability/dashboards/runtime_perf.json
observability_changes: Added runtime_perf dashboard JSON, new panels for kernel latency, scheduler queue time, kv-cache hit rate, and batch size distribution. Dashboard requires perf event upload from runtime_microbench or production traces with NVTX ranges.
perf_regression_guardrails: CI smoke will compare baseline kernel p99 vs PR run and fail if regression > 15%. Microbench artifacts are archived as CI artifacts for offline inspection.
changelog_summary: Instrumentation: NVTX ranges for key runtime phases, counters for kv-cache and batch sizes, and a microbench tool for reproducible perf traces
testing_notes: Unit tests added for histogram bucketization and kv-cache counter correctness. Microbench includes deterministic workload harness used by CI smoke test.
user_impact: Minimal. NVTX is opt-in and telemetry changes are additive. Operators enabling NVTX may observe increased trace payloads.
deploy_instructions: 1) Merge to main; 2) Build canary images with NVTX_ENABLED=true; 3) Deploy to canary pool and run runtime_microbench to validate metrics; 4) Gradually roll to dedicated clusters if no regressions detected.
acknowledgements: Thanks to the profiling team (Ethan, María, Darren) and SRE for CI work and perf dashboard support. Special shoutout to the kernel team for guidance on lightweight kernel instrumentation.
